record.original_question: Does there exist, in the space of metrics with conical singularities, a (continuous or smooth) family of metrics gt such that g0 is the round metric of the sphere, g1 is the metric from the example above, and σ(gt ) is a decreasing function of t.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let S² denote the 2-sphere. By a metric with conical singularities on S² we mean a length metric g induced by a Riemannian metric on the complement of finitely many points p₁,…,p_k ∈ S² such that, in suitable local coordinates around each p_i, g has the form of a flat (or smooth) cone of total angle θ_i ∈ (0,∞). For such a metric let

  sys(g) = inf{ length_g(γ) : γ is a non-constant closed geodesic on (S²,g) },

  area(g) = total 2-dimensional Hausdorff area of (S²,g),

and define the systolic ratio
  σ(g) = area(g) / sys(g)².

Two reference metrics:
 • g₀ is the round metric of constant curvature 1 on S² (no singularities); one has σ(g₀) = 4π/(2π)² · normalization giving σ(g₀) = 1/π.
 • g₁ is the flat metric on S² obtained by isometrically gluing two equilateral Euclidean triangles along their three pairs of corresponding edges; this is a flat metric with three conical singularities, each of cone angle 2π/3, and satisfies σ(g₁) = 1/(2√3).

Note that σ(g₁) < σ(g₀).

Question. Does there exist, in the space of metrics with conical singularities on S², a continuous (resp. smooth) one-parameter family {g_t}_{t∈[0,1]} of such metrics, joining g_0 to g_1, such that the function

  t ↦ σ(g_t)

is monotone decreasing on [0,1]?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears in a published list of open problems on geodesics (Burns–Matveev), attributed to Babenko, in the context of Calabi's conjectured optimal systolic ratio on S² realized by the flat metric glued from two equilateral triangles. No subsequent work resolving the existence of such a monotone interpolating family of conical metrics could be located; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems and questions about geodesics (Burns–Matveev)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey/problem list including systolic questions on S² with conical singularities, citing Calabi's two-equilateral-triangles example.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed in a problems list and is not marked as resolved.

status_evidence.title: A systolic inequality for geodesic flows on the two-sphere
status_evidence.snippet: Studies systolic ratios of metrics on S² but does not exhibit a monotone family of conical metrics from the round metric to Calabi's triangle example.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent systolic work on S² does not resolve the monotone-family question.
